gemini.rationale: The steel business's products (T4) and its manufacturing facilities/processes (T5) were transferred together, so there is no gap_45. However, historically shared corporate functions (treasury, IT, HR, etc.) did not transfer as an intact substrate, creating a gap_56 where the operational processes were separated from the parent's corporate organization. This gap was mitigated at closing via a transition services agreement and other ancillary agreements.

grok.rationale: gap_45 is 0 because the slice states the customer-facing steel portfolio (SBQ bars, seamless tubing, precision components) and the manufacturing facilities/processes that produce it (Akron/Canton/Eaton/Columbus/Houston plants, raw-material management, research/engineering, R&D) were both detached together into TimkenSteel at closing. gap_56 is 0 because that same operating package moved with its ~2,700 employees and the TimkenSteel executive team (who were to resign from Timken at completion); the TSA and ancillary agreements bridged only historically parent-shared corporate services (treasury, tax, accounting, IT/data-center, HR, legal), not a product-or-process transfer stripped of its operating organization.

openai.rationale: The entire customer-facing steel portfolio moved together with its manufacturing facilities, raw-material management, research and engineering functions, and distribution facilities, so no product-versus-process mismatch is documented at closing [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-201428, Form 10-12B EX-99.1]. The approximately 2,700-person operating workforce and steel-business management transferred, but historically shared corporate processes—including treasury, accounting, HR, IT, and legal services—did not transfer with their supporting organization; this gap was contractually absorbed through the transition services agreement and related IT-data-center arrangements [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-201428, Form 10-12B EX-99.1].
